alignments.note: Infinitive construct with no preposition before it: the English infinitive marker 'to' belongs to the infinitive's own unit (rule 52), headed on the lexical verb.
Nomen rectum takes the relational 'of' (rule 19); anarthrous substantival adjective takes the supplied 'the' (rule 46).
Predicate adjective takes the construction-supplied copula (rule 20); discontinuous around the negative under rule 25.

The negative's scope covers both cola and the ASV rewrites it at the head of the second as 'Nor', so both occurrences are this morpheme's one discontinuous unit under rule 25, headed on the first. No waw stands in the second colon to carry the coordination, so rule 35's fusion does not reach it; marking the italic 'Nor' added under rule 14 was the competing reading (rule 8).
Written 'to' for the preposition before the infinitive (rule 52). The margin's 'Or, So as to turn aside' is read and set aside (rule 38).
Verb with its phrasal particle; the head stays on the verb (rule 44).
Assimilated article segmented by MACULA; the ASV writes no 'the' before 'judgment' (rules 12, 29).

review_notes: The italic 'Nor' is read as the distributed second realization of the written לֹא (rule 25), since no conjunction morpheme stands in the second colon.
